title: Fainting or near-fainting
summary: Prevent a fall, use a safe position, and look for heart, stroke, bleeding, or persistent warning signs.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Presyncope
actions: Help a light-headed person sit or lie down immediately to prevent a fall.
If alert and there are no signs of heart attack or stroke, leg-crossing with strong leg and abdominal muscle tensing may help prevent fainting.
If the person faints, check breathing. If breathing normally and no serious trauma is suspected, keep them lying down; use the recovery position if alertness remains reduced.

Call emergency services if the person does not improve within 1 to 2 minutes, faints during exercise, has chest pain, breathing difficulty, stroke signs, severe bleeding, significant injury, or repeated episodes.
Do not let the person stand suddenly after recovery.
prohibitions: Do not sit or stand a faint person upright immediately.
Do not give food or drink until fully alert and able to swallow.
Do not use counterpressure manoeuvres when heart attack or stroke signs are present.
